title: Inject fields by key from a registry

blocks.text: The page's Q1 simulates Spring's field injection: every field that carries `@Inject` gets a value from a registry, looked up by a key. `@Inject("dataSource")` names the key; a bare `@Inject` has `value()` equal to `""`, and then **the field's own name is the key**. Private fields are injected too.
`KeyedInjector.Inject` (given) has `String value() default ""`. Write `KeyedInjector.inject(Object target, Map<String, Object> registry)`:

items: For each field that `target`'s class declares with `@Inject`, compute the key and, when the registry holds a value for it, set the field to that value.
**A key the registry does not hold leaves the field as it was**: a field that already had a value keeps it.
**Fields without `@Inject` are never touched**, even when the registry holds an entry under their name.

cases.says: Private @Inject("dataSource") and @Inject("pool") fields receive the registry's values for those keys, the very objects it holds, even when the registry also has an entry under the field's own name.
The page's InjectableService: a bare @Inject field named config receives the registry's "config" entry.
An @Inject field whose key the registry lacks, or maps to null, keeps the value it was initialised with.
A field without @Inject keeps its value although the registry holds an entry under its name.

concepts: Runtime processing reads RUNTIME annotations through reflection; a simple injector sets each @Inject field from a registry, keyed by the annotation's value or else the field's name.
Reflection reaches private members only after setAccessible(true).
